meta.title: Culla: a free Mac app for culling photos
meta.description: Culla finds the blinks, the blur and the lookalikes in a shoot with Apple’s Vision framework, on your Mac. You decide, one key at a time. Free, no account, nothing uploaded.

hero.title: Culla helps you pick the keepers.
hero.lead: It finds the blinks, the blur and the lookalikes with Apple’s Vision framework, which runs on your Mac’s Neural Engine. You decide, one key at a time.
hero.copiedSay: Link copied. Open it on your Mac.

how.title: How it works
how.step2: Culla sorts it into piles: duplicates, lookalikes, closed eyes, blurry, badly exposed.
how.step3: Press P to keep, X to reject. Nothing moves until you say so.

vision.title: Apple Vision on your Mac
vision.lead: Everything Culla finds comes from Apple’s own frameworks: Vision, Core Image and ImageIO. There are no third-party models.

vision.closing1: No model to download. No cloud. Your photos never leave your Mac.
vision.closing2: Culla suggests, you decide. Every flag shows why.

safe.title: Your photos stay yours
safe.rejects: Rejects go to a {folder} folder inside the shoot. Nothing is deleted.
safe.sidecar: Ratings and keep or reject marks can also be written to XMP sidecars beside your photos. Culla never changes an image file.

catch.title: So what’s the catch?
catch.note1: Culla started as a personal project: a tool I built for my own photos. It turned out to be worth sharing, so I’m sharing it. That’s the whole story.
catch.note2: No paid version is waiting behind this one. No ads, no account, and nothing collected about you or your photos. The code is open on {github} under the MIT licence, so you don’t have to take my word for any of it. If Culla is useful to you, good. If something is broken or missing, tell me.

todo.title: Not finished yet
todo.lead: Culla is new, and a few things are still rough.
todo.tuning: Detection settings are still being tuned on real shoots, so check what Culla flags before you apply.
todo.eyes: Closed eyes have been checked on only a few real faces so far. If Culla misses a blink, or sees one that isn’t there, tell me.
todo.sidecars: Writing XMP sidecars is still in beta.
todo.trash: Sending rejects to the Trash has had less testing than the {folder} folder.
todo.question: Ask a question
todo.githubNote: These open on GitHub, where you need a free account to write. Write in English, Russian or Turkmen.

systems.q: Which Macs and cameras does it work with?
systems.a: Any Mac with macOS 26 or later. Culla reads JPEG, HEIC and the RAW formats macOS itself can read.

internet.a: No. The app has no network access at all, so nothing is uploaded anywhere. Your photos stay on your Mac.

changes.a: No. Culla never changes an image file. Until you apply, your decisions are only marks. When you apply, files are moved, not edited.

rejects.a: When you apply, they move to a {folder} folder inside the shoot. In Settings you can send them to the Trash instead, or only mark them. Culla doesn’t delete anything, and Apply can be undone.

free.a: It started as a personal project, and I’m sharing it. There is no paid tier and there are no ads.

open.a: Yes. The code is on {github} under the MIT licence. You can read it, build it yourself, or {fix}.

counting.a: The server keeps an ordinary log to count visits. Like any web server's log, it records your IP address and browser, and it is deleted after 30 days. No cookies, no scripts watching you. The download itself comes from GitHub, which keeps its own count and its own logs.

report.q: How do I report a problem?
report.a: On GitHub, where you can {bug}, {feature} or {question}. You need a free GitHub account to write there.
